ordered_diagnoses: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion in a patient undergoing immunotherapy
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden vision loss and retinal vascular occlusion

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Combined occlusion of central retinal artery and vein was observed

shortlist.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Mild swelling of the optic disc and vision loss are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Optic disc swelling and vision loss could be related to this condition, especially in the context of immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Optic Neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Relative afferent pupillary defect and optic disc swelling are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, which could be related to lymphoma

shortlist.label: Metastatic Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing immunotherapy, which could increase the risk of metastatic cancer

shortlist.label: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
shortlist.why_kept: Vision loss, optic disc swelling, and retinal vascular occlusion could be related to this condition

raw.rationale: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm and immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein, which is consistent with lymphoma, particularly in the context of the patient's treatment with immunosuppressive agents and the presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm in the vitreous biopsy.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop occlusion of the central retinal artery, this is not the primary diagnosis as it does not explain the initial swelling of the optic disc and the findings on the vitreous biopsy.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
rejected.why: Similar to central retinal artery occlusion, this diagnosis does not account for the initial optic disc swelling and the biopsy results.

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: This condition could explain some of the patient's symptoms, but it does not account for the hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm found in the vitreous biopsy.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: Typically presents with headache, jaw claudication, and visual loss in older adults, which does not match this patient's profile.

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: Characterized by inflammation of the optic nerve, which could explain some symptoms, but the biopsy results suggest a neoplastic process rather than inflammation.

rejected.label: Metastatic Cancer
rejected.why: While possible, the biopsy results and immunohistochemistry suggest a primary CNS lymphoma rather than metastasis from another cancer.

rejected.label: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
rejected.why: This diagnosis would not explain the presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm in the vitreous biopsy.
